claim.date_text_original: Silla Village Register; proposed dates include 695, 755, 815, and 818–819 CE
claim.summary: The Silla Village Register records 25 nobi among 462 persons in four villages and distinguishes their status administratively from free people. Specialist and institutional syntheses interpret the register as direct evidence of private slavery in these communities. The wide 695–819 interval encodes disagreement over the date of the surviving register; it must not be read as a 125-year continuous observation.

territorial_practice.notes: P2 is restricted to the documented village-register communities. The register supports an institutional status category but cannot be extrapolated mechanically to all Unified Silla territory.

source.reliability_limitations: Some interpretive statements generalize beyond the four surviving village records; this atlas claim is therefore spatially restricted to the register communities.
